verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.164
17. Practice
Patient (1st)
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?

verses.pali: Akkhamā paṭipadā, khamā paṭipadā, damā paṭipadā, samā paṭipadā.
verses.english: Impatient practice, patient practice, taming practice, and calming practice.
And what’s the impatient practice?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akkosantaṁ paccakkosati, rosantaṁ paṭirosati, bhaṇḍantaṁ paṭibhaṇḍati.
verses.english: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with you, and you abuse, annoy, or argue right back at them.
This is called the impatient practice.
And what’s the patient practice?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akkosantaṁ na paccakkosati, rosantaṁ na paṭirosati, bhaṇḍantaṁ na paṭibhaṇḍati.
verses.english: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with you, and you don’t abuse, annoy, or argue back at them.
This is called the patient practice.
And what’s the taming practice?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī;
verses.english: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

verses.pali: yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ; cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving restraint over it.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

verses.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī;
verses.english: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

verses.pali: yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving restraint over it.
This is called the taming practice.
And what’s the calming practice?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti; uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ … uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, get rid of them, calm them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.
This is called the calming practice.
These are the four ways of practice.”
